review_notes: I read the whole file and compared it with the sibling Mathlib/Data/Finsupp/Interval.lean. The only repeated pattern is the step "if f i = 0 and g i = 0, then Icc (f i) (g i) is {0}, via Icc_self". It appears in the `support'` field of `rangeIcc` (lines 99-109) and in `support_rangeIcc_subset` (lines 116-123). The two uses are short, about 2-3 lines each. They also work at different levels: the first reasons with multisets and raw `support'` data, the second with Finset supports. A shared helper would save almost nothing and might complicate both. The Finsupp file defines `rangeIcc` differently, through `Finsupp.onFinset`/support equality, so it does not repeat the DFinsupp proof. The cardinality lemmas (`card_Ico`, `card_Ioc`, `card_Ioo`, `card_Iio`) are one-line rewrites using existing generic lemmas. I found no substantial repeated argument that a precise helper would improve.
